newsitem.title: JAPAN: INTERVIEW--Gourmet Kineya sees profits doubling.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW--Gourmet Kineya sees profits doubling.

text.p: Restaurant chain operator Gourmet Kineya Co Ltd expects its parent current profit to more than double to 4.3 billion yen in the 2000/01 business year from current levels, the company's president said.
In an interview, Hikoyuki Mukumoto also said that the company wanted to launch three new businesses by the end of the current business year to March 31, 1998.
These may include nationwide restaurant chains specialising in Italian or Japanese cuisine, he said.
He added that the Osaka-based restaurant operator hopes to spin off the new businesses and list them publicly.
"I think we may be able to get on track with these new businesses in three years and to offer their shares publicly in five years," Mukumoto said.

By the end of the year to March 2001, Gourmet Kineya aims to have a total of 680 restaurants serving western and Japanese food, and to post annual parent sales of 51.5 billion yen and a parent operating profit of 4.8 billion yen, Mukumoto said.
At the end of March 1997, Gourmet Kineya had 450 restaurants.

In 1996/97 Gourmet Kineya posted a parent current profit of 2.14 billion yen, up 15.1 percent from the previous year, and an operating profit of 2.28 billion yen, up 5.6 percent. Parent sales rose 6.9 percent to 30.59 billion yen.
Gourmet Kineya said in May that it expected to post a parent current profit of 2.37 billion yen in 1997/98 on sales of 33.95 billion yen. It did not provide a forecast for operating profits.
